title: Indicator correlation with linear forms
statement:
Let $n\in\mathbb N$, and let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ take only the values $0$ and $1$, with uniform expectation $\alpha=\mathbb E f>0$. For real coefficients $(a_i)_{i=1}^n$ satisfying $\sum_i a_i^2=1$, the squared correlation with the sign-valued linear form obeys
\[\left(\mathbb E\left[f(x)\sum_i a_i(-1)^{x_i}\right]\right)^2\le2\alpha^2\log(1/\alpha).\]
replaced: Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}$ have uniform mean $\alpha>0$, and let $a_i\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $\sum_ia_i^2=1$. Then $\big(\mathbb E[f(x)\sum_i a_i(-1)^{x_i}]\big)^2\le2\alpha^2\log(1/\alpha)$.
